articles.title: Supreme Court to commence final hearing of pleas on marital rape in December
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Under the exception clause of Section 375 of the Indian Penal Code, now repealed and replaced by the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, sexual intercourse or sexual acts by a man with his wife, the wife not being minor, is not rape
The Supreme Court on Thursday (November 19, 2026) said it would list a batch of petitions pertaining to the contentious issue of marital rape for final hearing in December.

The Supreme Court is seized of petitions raising the vexed legal question of whether a husband should enjoy immunity from prosecution for the offence of rape if he forces his wife, who is not a minor, to have sex.

Under the exception clause of Section 375 of the Indian Penal Code, now repealed and replaced by the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, sexual intercourse or sexual acts by a man with his wife, the wife not being minor, is not rape.
Even under the new law, exception 2 to Section 63 (rape) says that “sexual intercourse or sexual acts by a man with his own wife, the wife not being under eighteen years of age, is not rape”.
The petitions were listed for hearing during the day before a Bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana.

Senior advocate Indira Jaising, who is appearing in the matter, told the Supreme Court that the Bench is scheduled to hear a part-heard matter at 2 p.m. during the day. She urged the Bench that the marital rape matter be listed for hearing in December, as today it may not come up since the Bench is seized of a part-heard matter.
“We will either have it on December 2-3 or on December 9-10. Today, it is not possible. We are trying to finish the part-heard matter today,” the CJI said.
One of the lawyers appearing in the marital rape case requested the Bench to list the matter on December 9 and 10.
“We will fix it on December 9 or December 10,” the Bench said, adding, “We will try to hear it before the winter break”.
The winter break in the Supreme Court would commence from December 21.
On September 9, the Centre had told the Bench that the counter affidavit filed earlier by it in the lead case may be treated as its reply in other petitions as well.

The Bench had then observed that it would examine aspects such as whether prosecution can be sustained if the marital rape exception survives, and whether the exception itself was constitutionally valid.

articles.title: Author Samina Mishra explores borders, identity and citizenship through children’s eyes
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The filmmaker and author examines how art and storytelling can open up conversations about society, equality and constitutional values

What do borders mean to a child? Is it a line separating two countries, a language that makes someone feel like an outsider, or the invisible divisions that determine who belongs and who does not? For filmmaker and children’s author Samina Mishra, these questions have informed much of her work with children, particularly those growing up in circumstances where displacement, identity and belonging shape everyday life. Samina, who will be in Visakhapatnam for the Vizag Junior Literary Fest this month, believes that young people must have the space to question the divisions that shape their world.

Her engagement with these ideas took shape through a three-year association with Simurgh Centre in Delhi, where she conducted art workshops with children from Khirkee, a south Delhi neighbourhood home to several Afghan refugee families. The monthly Simurgh Children’s Art Workshop, designed for children aged nine to 15, offered them an opportunity to watch films, discuss their themes and respond through art. For children with limited access to spaces for play, leisure and creative expression, these sessions opened up possibilities for engaging with the world beyond their immediate circumstances.

During the first year, Samina selected short films from different countries, particularly those that communicated visually with little or no dialogue, allowing children from different linguistic backgrounds to participate. One of the films screened was The Present , a Palestinian short about a father and son attempting to buy a gift and the difficulties they encounter at checkpoints.
“It initiated conversations about lines and borders. That is also what my book Lines explores,” she says.

In her workshops for children, the idea of a line extends beyond geographical boundaries. Through discussions and art-based exercises, children examine the many ways people are separated, whether by language, caste, community or circumstances.

The conversations also draw from their experiences of moving to unfamiliar places and negotiating questions of identity and belonging. By encouraging children to approach these subjects through their own experiences, Samina hopes to make larger social questions more accessible.

Her interest in children’s understanding of society formed another project called ‘Hum Hindustani’, a research initiative she conceived and executed, which examines citizenship through the constitutional principles of liberty, equality and fraternity. Part of the Transforming Education for Sustainable Futures (TESF) India network, the project engages children in Grades 6 to 9 across three locations: Shaheen Bagh in Delhi, rural Firozpur in Punjab and Kitab Mahal, a library serving Dalit and Muslim children in Govandi, Mumbai.

Each location represents a distinct social and political experience, from the citizens’ protest at Shaheen Bagh to the farmers’ movement in Punjab and community-led learning initiatives in Govandi. Through arts-based exercises and documentary interviews with children and adults, the project explores how constitutional promises relate to the realities of growing up in different social settings.

“The initiative documents children’s creative responses through artwork and poetry,” says Samina. Its Hum Hindustani Poetry Podcast brings their writing into conversation with writers, artists and educators. Available in English and Hindi, the recordings offer an insight into how young people interpret citizenship through their everyday experiences.

For Samina, the project also addresses the marginalisation of children’s voices in conversations about democracy and society. “While children are frequently discussed in the context of education, welfare and public policy, their own interpretations receive far less attention,” she says and adds, “Children must be recognised as individuals capable of thinking about their rights, relationships and responsibilities.”

Currently, ‘Hum Hindustani’ is also engaging with children at Yellow Streets, a community learning space for those from vulnerable and underserved neighbourhoods, through workshops involving two animal films . Samina is also working on a picture book with Tulika Publishers.

At the Vizag Junior Literary Festival, scheduled for November 21 and 22 at Hawa Mahal in Visakhapatnam, Samina will conduct two sessions for children aged eight to 12 and 13 to 16. Each 90-minute session will draw on the workshops developed around the themes explored in Lines. Through creative exercises and conversations, participants will be encouraged to examine separation, identity and belonging from their own perspectives, without being led towards predetermined answers. At the literary festival, she hopes to encourage young participants to look beyond familiar definitions and consider a question that has occupied much of her work: what does it take to make room for everyone?

The conversations also draw from their experiences of moving to unfamiliar places and negotiating questions of identity and belonging. By encouraging children to approach these subjects through their own experiences, Samina hopes to make larger social questions more accessible.

Her interest in children’s understanding of society formed another project called ‘Hum Hindustani’, a research initiative she conceived and executed, which examines citizenship through the constitutional principles of liberty, equality and fraternity. Part of the Transforming Education for Sustainable Futures (TESF) India network, the project engages children in Grades 6 to 9 across three locations: Shaheen Bagh in Delhi, rural Firozpur in Punjab and Kitab Mahal, a library serving Dalit and Muslim children in Govandi, Mumbai.

Each location represents a distinct social and political experience, from the citizens’ protest at Shaheen Bagh to the farmers’ movement in Punjab and community-led learning initiatives in Govandi. Through arts-based exercises and documentary interviews with children and adults, the project explores how constitutional promises relate to the realities of growing up in different social settings.

“The initiative documents children’s creative responses through artwork and poetry,” says Samina. Its Hum Hindustani Poetry Podcast brings their writing into conversation with writers, artists and educators. Available in English and Hindi, the recordings offer an insight into how young people interpret citizenship through their everyday experiences.

For Samina, the project also addresses the marginalisation of children’s voices in conversations about democracy and society. “While children are frequently discussed in the context of education, welfare and public policy, their own interpretations receive far less attention,” she says and adds, “Children must be recognised as individuals capable of thinking about their rights, relationships and responsibilities.”

Currently, ‘Hum Hindustani’ is also engaging with children at Yellow Streets, a community learning space for those from vulnerable and underserved neighbourhoods, through workshops involving two animal films . Samina is also working on a picture book with Tulika Publishers.

At the Vizag Junior Literary Festival, scheduled for November 21 and 22 at Hawa Mahal in Visakhapatnam, Samina will conduct two sessions for children aged eight to 12 and 13 to 16. Each 90-minute session will draw on the workshops developed around the themes explored in Lines. Through creative exercises and conversations, participants will be encouraged to examine separation, identity and belonging from their own perspectives, without being led towards predetermined answers. At the literary festival, she hopes to encourage young participants to look beyond familiar definitions and consider a question that has occupied much of her work: what does it take to make room for everyone?

articles.title: BJP mocks Rahul Gandhi's U.S. remarks, says AI can predict his speeches
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The BJP also said that Congress should consider sending an AI-generated version of its leader abroad because he keeps repeating the same words

The BJP on Thursday (November 19, 2026) slammed Congress leader Rahul Gandhi for his remarks during his U.S. visit, accusing him of making “Hawai” allegations about India's electoral process and lowering the country's image on foreign soil.
The BJP also said that Congress should consider sending an AI-generated version of its leader abroad because he keeps repeating the same words.

Interacting with students at the University of Chicago on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), Mr. Gandhi said Indian democracy is “sacred”, and the Congress is ready to face electoral defeats until people realise that the system has been “completely demolished”.
Mr. Gandhi also said that boycotting elections over alleged flaws in the system would bring an end to Indian democracy, which the Congress does not intend to do.

Addressing a press conference at the party headquarters, BJP spokesperson and Rajya Sabha MP Sudhanshu Trivedi said it is unfortunate that Mr. Gandhi is making remarks against India in Chicago, the city where Swami Vivekananda had once brought glory to the country.
“Today, we have a leader of the opposition who is lowering the prestige of Mother India at the same place. This is unfortunate for the Congress and painful for Indians,” Mr. Trivedi said.
ALSO WATCH Watch: India facing ‘economic disaster’: Rahul Gandhi at Columbia university
He was responding to Mr. Gandhi's remarks questioning the 2024 Lok Sabha elections and concerns over electoral irregularities.

Referring to Mr. Gandhi's claim that a Brazilian model voted “23 times” in India, Mr. Trivedi questioned the basis of the charge. “Anyone coming from abroad should have an immigration record, shouldn't they? Just imagine, a leader of the opposition can make such ‘Hawai’ allegations,” he said.
Taking a swipe at Mr. Gandhi's frequent foreign visits, Mr. Trivedi said the Congress should stop spending money on sending him abroad.
“It is the age of AI now. They should simply send an AI-generated version of him because he has to repeat the same sentences and words again and again,” he said.
Mr. Trivedi also suggested that an AI model could be programmed with four options to generate his political remarks.

articles.title: Japanese PM Takaichi calls for continued dialogue with China to ease bilateral tensions
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Earlier in the day, Ms. Takaichi shook hands with Chinese President Xi Jinping and later held a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin

Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi on Thursday (November 19, 2026) called for continued dialogue and communication with China to ease bilateral tensions triggered by her remarks on Taiwan, saying Beijing is an "important neighbour" with which Tokyo has several outstanding issues.
Ms. Takaichi is in Shenzhen to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting.

"China is an important neighbour, and between the two countries there are outstanding issues, and that is why it is important to continue communicating and having dialogue,” she told the media on the sidelines of the APEC summit.
Earlier in the day, Ms. Takaichi shook hands with Chinese President Xi Jinping and later held a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
When asked about her brief interaction with Mr. Xi, the Japanese PM said she thanked him for the invitation and congratulated him on successfully hosting the APEC summit.

Relations between Tokyo and Beijing have sharply deteriorated after Takaichi told parliament in November last year that a Chinese attack on Taiwan, a self-governed island claimed by China, could trigger a situation in which Japan's Self-Defence Forces might support US forces.
Her remarks infuriated China, prompting it to take a series of political and economic measures against Japan, including export restrictions on rare earths used in a wide range of high-tech products.
Asked about the controversy, Ms. Takaichi said Japan's four political documents governing its relations with China remained unchanged and continued to serve as the foundation of bilateral ties.

Tokyo will continue to advance a comprehensive strategic relationship of mutual benefit with Beijing while pursuing dialogue to protect their respective national interests and build constructive and stable ties, she said, according to the Hong Kong-based South China Morning Post.
Ms. Takaichi refrained from commenting on a hypothetical Taiwan contingency, saying Japan's position on Taiwan, as articulated in the 1972 Japan-China Joint Communique, remained unchanged.
China and Japan have counterclaims over the Senkaku Islands in the East China Sea, which Beijing calls the Diaoyu Islands.
Replying to queries on her meeting with Mr. Putin, Ms. Takaichi said she raised Tokyo's concerns over Russia's detention of Japanese nationals and the treatment of Japanese companies.

articles.title: Xi-Trump-Putin trilateral meeting LIVE: Ukraine strikes Crimean bridge again as Trump says U.S., China want to help end war
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: China-U.S. relations 'stable and improved', Xi says; Trilateral summit to begin shortly on the sidelines of the ongoing APEC Summit

Some in the West are comparing the three-way meeting to the 1945 Yalta conference, where the wartime leaders of the U.S., Britain and the Soviet Union divided Germany and Berlin, carved out zones of influence in Europe, and agreed to establish the United Nations.
The Kremlin, which long has courted the concept of a “multipolar world” offering an equal say to all nations, plays down the Yalta comparisons, which are also unwelcome to China for similar reasons.

Fyodor Lukyanov, a pro-Kremlin foreign policy expert, noted that even as Moscow publicly rejects the Yalta analogy, it seems to believe the leaders could “reach agreements and make decisions that will determine global developments”.
Of the three nations, “it seems that only Russia really believes in the possibility of global control”, he told a recent roundtable.

Chatham House director Bronwen Maddox said in a commentary that “standing with Xi and Trump, Putin will look like one of the three main leaders of the world”, even though “Russia is no superpower” and its economy, overloaded with military spending, is dwindling.
She warned that “the danger for Ukraine is that Trump uses this summit to try to advance his notion of peace, including giving Russia territory it has not managed to seize by force”.

The meeting follows US-mediated peace talks between Russia and Ukraine held in Abu Dhabi last week for the first time in nine months. The negotiations produced few visible results as the parties stuck to their sharply divergent demands. -- AP
Trilateral Xi-Putin-Trump summit draws Yalta 1945 comparisons, highlighting postwar order shifts amid Ukraine tensions and multipolar world debates.

Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday (November 19, 2026) told U.S. President Donald Trump and China’s Xi Jinping that their three countries shared an “interest” in resolving the Ukraine war and a “responsibility” for global peace and security.

“Our countries have many converging interests when it comes to resolving regional conflicts, including, of course, the conflict in Ukraine,” Mr. Putin said in opening remarks at a landmark summit between the three leaders in Shenzhen.

He added they had a “shared responsibility for maintaining international peace and security” and that closed-door discussions would also touch on food and energy security - both of which have been upended by the Iran and Ukraine wars.- AFP

China, the United States and Russia should “jointly safeguard world peace and stability”, Xi Jinping told Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin as the three leaders met in the Chinese city of Shenzhen on Thursday (November 19, 2026).

articles.title: Muslims to outnumber Christians by 2035 worldwide: Pew research
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The absolute number of Hindus in India and worldwide will rise from 1.2 billion in 2020 to 1.4 billion by 2070

Islam is projected to be the world's largest religion by 2035, surpassing Christianity, according to a new study released by the Pew Research Centre on Wednesday (November 18, 2026). Pew said if current trends continue, there will be more than 3.6 billion Muslims and just under three billion Christians worldwide by 2070.
The absolute number of Hindus in India and worldwide will rise from 1.2 billion in 2020 to 1.4 billion by 2070.

But the rest of the world's population -- all non-Hindus -- will grow at an even faster rate. As a result, Hindus will shrink slightly as a share of the global population, falling from 15% in 2020 to 14% in 2070.
The world's total population is projected to increase by 29% between 2020 and 2070, with Christians growing by 30% and Muslims by 80%.
"The largest source of new members of major religions is not adults who convert to the faith, but babies who are born into the group," the Pew projections found.

During 2020-2025, the fertility rate for Muslims was 3.1 children per woman, followed by the rate for Christians at 2.5, Pew said. The average fertility rate for all other women was 1.6, below the 2.1 level considered necessary for each generation to replace itself.
If current demographic trends continue, the number of Hindus in India will increase by 176 million between 2020 and 2070.

While India's overall fertility rate has fallen rapidly in recent decades, Muslims in India still have more children per woman than Hindus do, the Pew Research found. As per the Pew projections, Hindus comprise 79.4% of India's religious composition in 2020 and the number is set to slide to 75.8% by 2070.

Muslims comprise 15.2% of India's religious composition in 2020, and that share is set to rise to 19.6% by 2070. Outside India, much of the projected growth among Hindus will come from Pakistan (over five million) and the United States (over four million).
According to the Pew projections, the U.S. will have the world's fifth-largest Hindu population. Nepal and India will remain the only two countries with a Hindu majority.
It forecasts that Buddhists will shrink both in number and as a share of the world's population, partly due to expected declines in the overall populations of China, South Korea, and Japan.

If recent trends continue, by 2070 more than half of the world's Christians will live in sub-Saharan Africa. The Democratic Republic of the Congo will surpass the United States as the country with the largest Christian population.

articles.title: Xi, Trump, Putin exchange greetings before historic China summit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The agenda for the November 19 meeting between Presidents Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin -- which has raised fears of a carve-up into new "spheres of influence" -- was unclear

The leaders of China, the United States and Russia exchanged greetings as they met in Shenzhen on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), a day before their history-making first formal trilateral summit in the Chinese city.

The agenda for Thursday's (November 19, 2026) meeting between Presidents Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin -- which has raised fears of a carve-up into new "spheres of influence" -- was unclear, however.
And the three-way meeting was set to last "no more than an hour", Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told Russian state media Wednesday (November 18, 2026).

When Mr. Trump touched down in Shenzhen, Mr. Xi became the first Chinese paramount leader in decades to welcome a foreign leader as he arrived, mirroring the U.S. President's gesture at Joint Base Andrews in September.
Mr. Trump descended the stairs from his plane to be met by Mr. Xi, as well as renditions of both countries' national anthems and fighter jets that flew overhead and left colourful vapour trails.
The pair strolled down a red carpet lined with people waving pom-poms, brandishing Chinese and U.S. national flags, and shouting: "A warm welcome to you!"
A motorcade of dark limousines later carried Mr. Trump into the city, where the streets had been cleared of traffic, an AFP reporter observed.

Mr. Xi, Mr. Trump, Mr. Putin and other leaders attending the broader Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit then gathered for a welcome dinner, and the three briefly exchanged greetings before a group photo.

"I look forward to an in-depth exchange of views with you on major issues concerning China-U.S. relations, Asia-Pacific cooperation, and the global landscape, with the aim of advancing a constructive, strategically stable relationship between our two nations," Mr. Xi told Trump, according to Chinese state news agency Xinhua .

Washington had signalled that the Ukraine war -- something Mr. Xi vehemently sees as not China's problem -- was not expected to be addressed in the trilateral meeting, before Mr. Trump said that it would.
The summit is expected to include discussions of the Iran war and nuclear disarmament, according to Washington, after a U.S.-Russia bilateral treaty on atomic weapons expired in February.
Beijing has long maintained that the U.S. and Russia should reduce their giant nuclear arsenals before it agrees to talks on its smaller stockpile.

articles.title: GTA VI goes live: Inside Rockstar Games’ biggest video game yet
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: After a 13-year wait, GTA VI is finally here. Built on an estimated $1.5 billion, the game takes players into Leonida’s crime-filled world. Here’s a closer look

Putting an end to the long waiting period of over 13 years, the Grand Theft Auto (GTA) VI by Rockstar Games went live on Thursday (November 19, 2026) for millions of gamers across the globe, offering a gripping landscape of blazing action sequences and adventure-packed missions. The Rockstar Games’ biggest video game, widely reported to be the most expensive cultural product ever made of around $1.5 billion, has released on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S. The plot is set in Leonida (a Florida-inspired city), buzzing with traffic, crime and sun-drenched beaches, pairing spectacular visuals with the rise of two small-time criminals through the city’s underworld.

The central characters are a criminal couple, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, whose action-packed adventures punctuated by slow-motion effects and dramatic camera shifts is expected to the highlight of the videogame. Lucia has recently been released from prison, while Jason is a former soldier who became involved with drug runners in the Leonida Keys. When a criminal job goes wrong, the pair become entangled in a wider conspiracy.
Based on the latest reports, the videogame is not on the cards for the official release in Russia, China, Lebanon or Qatar.

As per the official site, over 4,700 employees cutting across a dozen studios of Rockstar studios, devoted more than eight years to build the latest instalment of GTA. The active production only began after the release of Rockstar’s previous game, Red Dead Redemption II, in 2018. Earlier slated for a late 2025 release , the game’s launch was postponed twice owing to a series of leaks in 2022 and the online release of stolen gameplay videos.

Developers immersed themselves in the region while building the game, driving through Miami, the Florida Keys and surrounding communities, flying over the Everglades and researching the area’s history and architecture.

In a bid to cater to the immersive gameplay experience, the videogame allows players to tune into more than 20 radio stations at home or in their vehicles, with music ranging from Simple Minds and Daft Punk to Van Halen. A fresh addition in the latest instalment is podcasts. Among the options is a true-crime-style series chronicling Vice City, the game’s main metropolis.

The videogame’s plot unfolds by building the relationship between Jason and Lucia, from a chance encounter during a police stop to a robbery gone wrong that lands Lucia in jail. Much of the adventure transpires through lengthy cinematic cut-scenes, allowing players to sit back and watch the story. Only later does the game open up and hand players control of Jason’s day-to-day life, a former soldier working for local gangsters, who is recovering drug packages dropped at sea, stealing cars and shaking down debtors.

The videogame’s release has sparked a wave of excitement among gamers for detailed attention to the graphics. In GTA VI, the hair sways in the wind, muscles flex beneath clothing and characters move with a naturalism. The fictional state of Leonida, Rockstar’s take on Florida, enables a larger-than-life experience to the gamers. This is enveloped by bustling city streets, neon-soaked nightlife and pristine beaches all feature in a vast 3D world that players can explore while scuba diving.

Further, the game’s map is learnt to be one of the biggest and busiest ever made in the GTA-series history. The latest addition allows the non-player characters go about their own lives, and the world seems to carry on whether the player is involved or not. A simple drive across town might involve a random police traffic stop, witnessing a car accident or stumbling across a robbery by the beach.

Additionally, players are likely to find cars heavier in the latest instalment of the video-game, relatably tough to manoeuvre with a responsibility to keep an eye on their fuel tanks. They also decide what stays in a car trunk and what comes along for the ride, juggle phone calls and messages, and use apps to identify targets or track potential scores.
Likewise, the police are seemed to be stricter than previous GTA games, expected to make a player more vigilant about their actions.
The series’ trademark humour is still there, whether in Jason and Lucia’s witty chats or through colourful side characters like Cal Hampton, a conspiracy-obsessed and slightly paranoid sidekick.

articles.title: India missed its 2025 TB elimination target. What does the WHO report show?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The WHO’s Global Tuberculosis Report 2026 has withheld India’s 2025 incidence estimate pending an assessment of new surveillance data. What does the report reveal about India’s TB burden, and why has the country missed its target?

The story so far: India continues to account for nearly a quarter of the world’s tuberculosis (TB) burden despite expanded diagnosis and treatment services, falling short of the national target of eliminating TB by 2025. According to the World Health Organization’s (WHO) Global Tuberculosis Report, released on November 12, 2026, an estimated 10.6 million people developed TB worldwide in 2025.

While India’s estimated TB mortality rate fell by 38%, from 28 deaths per lakh population in 2015 to 18 per lakh in 2025, the country diagnosed and notified 25.3 lakh cases during the year. However, the WHO has not published India’s estimated incidence for that year, as the figures are under review.

Science, Space & Environment Report: India missed its 2025 TB elimination target. What does the WHO report show?. This milestone highlights indigenous research, technological self-reliance, and environmental sustainability.

Scientific & Technical Core: Innovations led by ISRO, DRDO, CSIR, and national research institutes are advancing India's capabilities in space exploration, quantum computing, biotechnology, and clean energy.

articles.title: India, Japan discuss economic security, deeper business, people-to-people ties
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Jaishankar flagged the growing “weaponisation” of connectivity, resources, services, supply chains and market shares, saying many of these developments had direct implications for national security

India and Japan on Thursday (November 19, 2026) discussed strengthening economic security and deepening government-to-government, business-to-business and people-to-people linkages as External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar held talks with his Japanese counterpart Toshimitsu Motegi.
The meeting, held in Tokyo, was the 19th India-Japan Foreign Ministers' Strategic Dialogue.

In a post on X after the talks, Mr. Jaishankar said, "Glad to hold the 19th Foreign Ministers’ Strategic Dialogue with FM @moteging of Japan. Reviewed the entire gamut of our bilateral cooperation, focusing on strengthening economic security and deepening G2G, B2B and P2P linkages.”
“Our discussions also covered challenges and opportunities in the Indo-Pacific, regional hotspots, global issues, and multilateral cooperation," the Minister added.
Earlier, Mr. Jaishankar joined Mr. Motegi for the unveiling of a logo to mark the 75th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between India and Japan in 2027.

On Thursday (November 19, 2026), Mr. Jaishankar and Defence Minister Rajnath Singh also participated in the fourth India-Japan Foreign and Defence Ministers' Dialogue, known as the 2+2 meeting, in Tokyo.

Addressing the media after the meeting, Mr. Jaishankar flagged the growing “weaponisation” of connectivity, resources, services, supply chains and market shares, saying many of these developments had direct implications for national security.
He said India and Japan were committed to keeping the Indo-Pacific free and open and were joined in that endeavour by other Quad partners.
Mr. Jaishankar, on Thursday (November 19, 2026), also met Taro Aso, vice-president of Japan's Liberal Democratic Party.

In a post on X, Mr. Jaishankar said the two agreed on the need to strengthen their strategic, economic and energy security cooperation. He also said he valued Aso's commitment towards deepening the partnership between the two countries across governments, businesses and people.

articles.title: Bihar Chief Minister likely to begin statewide journey from November 26
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: During his journey, Mr. Choudhary is likely to spend a day in each district; reviewing development projects and the implementation of various government schemes. Bihar has total 38 districts.

Following the footsteps of his predecessor and former Chief Minister Nitish Kumar, Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary is likely to launch his statewide journey on November 26, 2026, from the West Champaran district.
During his journey, he is expected to review government schemes and development projects on the ground by meeting district officials, ministers in charge, and local residents.
Replacing Mr. Kumar, Mr. Choudhary of the Bharatiya Janata Party, for the first time in the party, became Bihar Chief Minister in April this year.
The Chief Minister is also likely to meet local residents and inaugurate and lay foundation stones for new development projects.

“The tentative date for the Chief Minister’s statewide journey is November 26. However, everything is still being finalised. While his participation in the journey is confirmed, final details are being given the finishing touches,” a senior official of the Chief Minister’s office, who wanted to be anonymous, told The Hindu.

The Bihar CM’s proposed journey is to begin after Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit to Bihar on November 21, 2026. During the visit, Mr. Modi is scheduled to inaugurate the six-lane ‘Nitish Setu’ from Kacchi Dargah-Bidupur in Vaishali district, and lay the foundation stone for other projects at Jaffarpatti industrial area under Rajapakar block of the Vaishali district.

Mr. Choudhary, along with other ministers in his cabinet, has been regularly reviewing the venues and holding meetings with senior officials ahead of the Prime Minister’s visit. Other BJP leaders of the State are also camping and holding meetings with local residents to make the PM’s visit, on the completion of one year of the NDA government in the State, a grand success.

articles.title: Malaysia to end visa-free entry to Indians from January 1, 2027
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Earlier, Indian nationals travelling to the South East Asian nation were granted a 30-day visa exemption and just had to register for Malaysia Digital Arrival Card within three days before arrival
Malaysia is ending its visa-free access for Indian nationals from January 1, 2027, the Immigration Department of Malaysia has announced.
Earlier, Indian nationals travelling to the South East Asian nation were granted a 30-day visa exemption and just had to register for Malaysia Digital Arrival Card within three days before arrival.
The visa exemption was introduced on December 1, 2023, and later extended to the end of 2026.
The Immigration Department of Malaysia (JIM), in a notice on November 17, said the visa exemption facility for Indian nationals will no longer be available with effect from 1 January 2027.

Accordingly, Indian nationals entering Malaysia from this date onwards will be required to obtain a valid visa prior to their arrival, it said. Visa applications may be submitted through the MyVISA portal starting 1 December 2026, it added.
The JIM further said that visa processing fees would be non-refundable, regardless of the application outcome, change of policy or any subsequent changes to travel plans.
The Immigration Department of Malaysia reserves the right to amend these entry requirements at any time in accordance with directives from the Government of Malaysia, the notice said.

It also advised visitors to obtain travel medical coverage for the full duration of their intended stay in Malaysia. Medical treatment and related healthcare services are chargeable to non-residents, who are responsible for all expenses incurred, it said.
In September, India had advised its nationals in Malaysia not to use the country's 30-day visa-free entry facility to seek employment.

In an advisory posted on X , the High Commission of India in Kuala Lumpur said it has noticed a “noticeable increase” in Indian nationals arriving in Malaysia who are "misled by unscrupulous agents with false job promises." The High Commission said the 30-day visa-free facility is meant for tourism and social visits and does not permit employment.

articles.title: T.N. BJP chief Nainar Nagenthran slams TVK govt. over alleged halting of ₹1,000 assistance to women
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The TVK-led government had denied the claim that the assistance has been halted

BJP State unit president Nainar Nagenthran on Thursday (November 19, 2026) accused the TVK government of betraying the women of Tamil Nadu by allegedly stopping the monthly ₹1,000 assistance to lakhs of beneficiaries under the Kalaignar Magalir Urimai Thogai scheme.

Citing media reports in this regard, he said more than 50% of the 16.94 lakh beneficiaries added during the second phase in December 2025 had reportedly not received the assistance for the past three months. The scheme had earlier benefited 1.31 crore women every month, he said.
Demanding that the government immediately credit the three months’ arrears to the affected beneficiaries, Mr. Nagenthran urged it to implement the promised ₹2,500 assistance without further delay.
It may be mentioned that the TVK-led government had denied the claim that the assistance has been halted.

articles.title: Telangana BIE releases Intermediate exam 2027 time table
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Theory examinations for Intermediate first-year students will commence on February 24, 2027, while second-year examinations will begin on February 25

The Telangana Board of Intermediate Education (TGBIE) on Thursday (November 19, 2026) announced the tentative schedule for the Intermediate Public Examinations (IPE) February/March 2027 for first and second-year students.

Theory examinations for Intermediate first-year students will commence on February 24, 2027, while second-year examinations will begin on February 25. All theory examinations will be conducted from 9 a.m. to 12 noon

Practical examinations for second-year science students will be held from February 1 to February 10, including Sundays. The examinations will be conducted in two sessions from 9 a.m. to 12 noon and 2 p.m. to 5 p.m.

For first-year science students, practical examinations will take place from February 11 to February 18, in three sessions from 9 a.m. to 11 a.m., 12 noon to 2 p.m., and 3.30 p.m. to 5:30 p.m. English practical examinations for first-year students are scheduled for January 29, and second-year students will appear for the examination on January 30.

Compulsory examinations such as Environmental Education is on January 27, and Ethics and Human Values is on January 29. As per the schedule, first-year internal assessment will be held from January 20 to 25.

The first-year theory examinations will begin with the second language Paper-I on February 24, followed by English Paper-I on February 26. The second-year examinations will commence with second language Paper-II on February 25, followed by English Paper-II on February 27.
The examinations conclude on March 20. The dates will also apply to Intermediate vocational course examinations, and a separate timetable will be issued, the Board said..

articles.title: Keralam mulling community-based system for early identification of at-risk children, providing support
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: FOLKS – Friends of Little Kids is envisaged as a structured child protection early warning and intervention initiative that aims at connecting vulnerable children with the formal child protection system without delays.

In the wake of the death of a toddler at Nedumangad following physical trauma, allegedly inflicted by his mother’s partner, Keralam is considering putting in place a community-based mechanism for early identification of children at risk and connecting them with the formal child protection system without delays.

FOLKS – Friends of Little Kids is envisaged as a structured child protection early warning and intervention initiative that focusses on children who may be facing abuse, neglect, abandonment, or other forms of harm but go unnoticed until very late, besides children who show violent behaviour.

The Statewide mechanism aims at strengthening connections between communities and existing institutional framework such as child welfare committees, district child protection units, Childline, and educational and health institutions to enable timely reporting of situations where children are at risk and support interventions such as rescue and rehabilitation.
FOLKS will tap into the network of Social Work students and faculty members and professionally qualified social work practitioners who work in the child protection and welfare sectors.

These FOLKS members will observe and report physical or emotional abuse, repeated injuries, severe neglect, malnutrition or starvation, child labour, child marriage risks, unsafe living conditions, dropping out of schools, and similar other situations.
The reporting will be done through Childline 1098, district child protection units (DCPUs), designated district-level WhatsApp groups, and child protection nodal officers.
The WhatsApp groups will include DCPU officials, Childline representatives, police nodal officers, social work college coordinators, and FOLKS representatives.

As serious incidents usually occur in households already experiencing social distress, DCPUs may maintain a confidential vulnerable family support register. Families with severe vulnerability, domestic violence, substance abuse, repeated police intervention, family breakdown, child neglect complaints, and previous child protection interventions will be identified through referrals from stakeholders in the existing child protection institutional framework.

A monitoring network including anganwadi workers, school teachers, DCPUs, and FOLKS members will all have roles such as observation of children; monitoring attendance and behavioural changes; reporting neglect, malnutrition, and safety concerns; conducting welfare visits; case management, and follow-up interventions.

Mentorship is an important aspect of the FOLKS initiative, particularly in the case of children in child care institutions. Regular communication with the children will allow the social work students to build a rapport with them and identify behavioural changes if any and bring about a modification in their behaviour. This will be particularly helpful once the department conducts vulnerability mapping to identify children in high-risk environments. The social work students in turn will be awarded certificates or some other token of appreciation for their work.
Inter-department coordination will be a significant aspect of FOLKS, which will be piloted in some districts before being extended across the State.

The Statewide mechanism aims at strengthening connections between communities and existing institutional framework such as child welfare committees, district child protection units, Childline, and educational and health institutions to enable timely reporting of situations where children are at risk and support interventions such as rescue and rehabilitation.

FOLKS will tap into the network of Social Work students and faculty members and professionally qualified social work practitioners who work in the child protection and welfare sectors.

These FOLKS members will observe and report physical or emotional abuse, repeated injuries, severe neglect, malnutrition or starvation, child labour, child marriage risks, unsafe living conditions, dropping out of schools, and similar other situations.

The reporting will be done through Childline 1098, district child protection units (DCPUs), designated district-level WhatsApp groups, and child protection nodal officers.

The WhatsApp groups will include DCPU officials, Childline representatives, police nodal officers, social work college coordinators, and FOLKS representatives.

As serious incidents usually occur in households already experiencing social distress, DCPUs may maintain a confidential vulnerable family support register. Families with severe vulnerability, domestic violence, substance abuse, repeated police intervention, family breakdown, child neglect complaints, and previous child protection interventions will be identified through referrals from stakeholders in the existing child protection institutional framework.

A monitoring network including anganwadi workers, school teachers, DCPUs, and FOLKS members will all have roles such as observation of children; monitoring attendance and behavioural changes; reporting neglect, malnutrition, and safety concerns; conducting welfare visits; case management, and follow-up interventions.

Mentorship is an important aspect of the FOLKS initiative, particularly in the case of children in child care institutions. Regular communication with the children will allow the social work students to build a rapport with them and identify behavioural changes if any and bring about a modification in their behaviour. This will be particularly helpful once the department conducts vulnerability mapping to identify children in high-risk environments. The social work students in turn will be awarded certificates or some other token of appreciation for their work.

Inter-department coordination will be a significant aspect of FOLKS, which will be piloted in some districts before being extended across the State.

Some in the West are comparing the three-way meeting to the 1945 Yalta conference, where the wartime leaders of the U.S., Britain and the Soviet Union divided Germany and Berlin, carved out zones of influence in Europe, and agreed to establish the United Nations.
The Kremlin, which long has courted the concept of a “multipolar world” offering an equal say to all nations, plays down the Yalta comparisons, which are also unwelcome to China for similar reasons.

She warned that “the danger for Ukraine is that Trump uses this summit to try to advance his notion of peace, including giving Russia territory it has not managed to seize by force”.

articles.title: China-Russia-U.S. trilateral summit: Xi, Putin, Trump call for cooperation to confront global security challenges
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The three heads of state — Xi Jinping, Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump — had an in-depth exchange of views on the current international situation and committed to maintaining strategic stability and international security

Chinese President Xi Jinping met Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump in Shenzhen on Thursday (November 19, 2026). Following the meeting, the three leaders reviewed the main areas of consensus reached during their discussions.
Shenzhen trilateral summit: Follow LIVE updates on November 19, 2026

“I’m delighted that this trip has given us the opportunity for this first ever trilateral meeting between the leaders of the United States, Russia, and China, and today, in that sense, we are really making history,” said Mr. Trump.
Mr. Xi said today’s meeting among the leaders had been positive, constructive and productive, and that the three countries shared common views on safeguarding world peace.

“We all remember the history of fighting side by side during the Second World War and emphasise the importance of cherishing the hard-won peace that emerged from it. We all agree that major powers should take seriously the legitimate security concerns of all countries. We all believe that dialogue and negotiation are the correct ways to resolve differences. As long as dialogue does not cease and doors remain open, there is hope for peace,” said Mr. Xi.
The three heads of State had an in-depth exchange of views on the current international situation and committed to maintaining strategic stability and international security.

“We have a special responsibility to maintain open, respectful, and productive dialogue on issues impacting not just our people but the entire planet. Too often, past leaders avoided talking to nations with whom they had disagreements, and we feel the opposite. No peace was ever forged by declining opportunities for engagement and speech,” said Mr. Trump.

The three heads of state recognised that the principle of state consent and respect for the immunities of state officials are of paramount importance, and concurred that the International Criminal Court and other similar bodies must not abuse their jurisdiction.
The three heads of state reaffirmed that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought.

“As the world’s three largest nuclear powers by far, the United States, Russia and China are uniquely positioned to discuss how to reduce the number of nuclear weapons on earth and also to lessen the risk that those weapons will ever be used, the power is unbelievable, unthinkable. In addition to exploring the potential for arms reduction in our own countries, and I must say it’s quite frankly a very hard thing to do, because once you have the nuclear weapons it’s very hard to not have them, it’s very hard to give them up as the leader of a country,” said Mr. Trump.
The three countries will conduct a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons.

“We all believe that cooperation is the only viable path for addressing challenges. Based on our shared interests, we should strengthen cooperation, promote peace through cooperation, and pursue win-win outcomes. The seeds planted by today’s meeting among our three countries will surely take root, blossom and bear fruit. China, Russia and the United States should faithfully implement the consensus reached at this meeting, continue to strengthen communication, build consensus through dialogue, confront challenges with a sense of responsibility, and work together to build a better world,” said Mr. Xi.

articles.title: Top UN court finds that Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya: Refugee crisis, timeline of the case, and more
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The ICJ had for seven years weighed the accusations made by Gambia against Myanmar’s treatment of its minority Rohingya community.

Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority, the International Court of Justice said on Thursday (November 19, 2026) in an historic verdict, the first time it has ruled a state committed the crime.

“The Republic of the Union of Myanmar has committed genocide against the Rohingya group in northern Rakhine State, in violation of its obligations under the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide,” said ICJ President Yuji Iwasawa.

Judges at the top UN court (also called the World Court) had for seven years been weighing accusations made by Gambia about whether Myanmar’s treatment of the Rohingya people breached the 1948 UN Genocide Convention.
The international community closely watched the verdict as an archetype for the case filed by South Africa against Israel over its campaign in Gaza.
The Rohingya are a minority ethnic group, largely comprising Muslims, in the predominantly Buddhist Myanmar, formerly referred to as Burma.

Most of the Rohingya come from the Rakhine State, also known as Arakan State, in northwest Myanmar. The State borders Bangladesh. They speak a dialect of Bengali, as opposed to the commonly spoken Burmese language. While the Rohingya people have been living in Myanmar for generations, they are not recognised by the country, rendering them effectively stateless. Their movement are also restricted within the Rakhine State.
When Burma won Independence from the UK in 1948, the Bengali-speaking Muslim population near the border exceeded that of the Buddhists, leading to secessionist tensions, according to Reuters .

In 1962, a coup led to nearly five decades of military rule by the ethnic Burman majority. In 1978, thousands of people fled to Bangladesh to escape a military census of the Rohingya called “Operation Dragon.”
In 1991, another wave of refugees fled to Bangladesh where the UN says 300,000 Rohingya now live a stateless existence.
From 2025: Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh mark anniversary of Myanmar exodus as conference opens

Due to years of harassment beginning in 2012 and exacerbated in 2017, thousands of Rohingya have fled Myanmar, with many attempting to travel in rickety wooden boats to Malaysia, where 14,300 official Rohingya refugees and maybe half as many unregistered ones live.

Sectarian violence between Rohingyas and Rakhine’s Buddhist natives began flaring up in June 2012, following the rape and murder of a Rakhine woman in a Rohingya-dominated locality, according to a report published in The Hindu. The riots, which were triggered as a result, went on for almost a month with causalities on both the sides.

fullParagraphs: Myanmar’s soldiers killed and raped Rohingya, committed violence against children, and destroyed Rohingya villages and settlements, the top UN court said

Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority, the International Court of Justice (ICJ) said on Thursday (November 19, 2026) in a historic verdict, the first time it has ruled a state committed the crime.

“The Republic of the Union of Myanmar has committed genocide against the Rohingya group in northern Rakhine State, in violation of its obligations under the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide,” said ICJ President Yuji Iwasawa.

Myanmar’s ​security forces killed ‌thousands of members ​of ⁠the Rohingya minority Muslim population and committed ‌widespread sexual violence, judges ‌at the World ‌Court ⁠ruled on ⁠Thursday (November 19, 2026).

The death toll announcement came early in a three-hour sitting to read out the International Court of Justice’s decision on whether Myanmar committed genocide in a brutal offensive against the Rohingya nearly a decade ago.

Judges ruled ‌that actions ‌by ‌Myanmar ⁠against ⁠the Rohingya in 2017 had ​the “intention ‌to destroy” a substantial ‌part of ​the Muslim minority population, ⁠meeting the ‌legal threshold for genocide.
Myanmar’s soldiers killed and raped Rohingya, committed violence against children, and destroyed Rohingya villages and settlements, the top UN court said.

They “killed thousands of Rohingya civilians, perpetrated widespread acts of sexual violence as well as acts of extreme violence against children, and attacked fleeing Rohingya as they sought to flee in large numbers to Bangladesh,” said Mr. Iwasawa.
The ICJ has not yet ruled whether Myanmar has committed the crime of genocide, in a landmark ruling that is expected to take around three hours to read out.
“The court has also determined that the estimate of 10,000 Rohingya violently killed during (2017) clearance operations is supported by the evidence,” said Mr. Iwasawa.

Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority, the International Court of Justice (ICJ) said on Thursday (November 19, 2026) in a historic verdict, the first time it has ruled a state committed the crime.

“The Republic of the Union of Myanmar has committed genocide against the Rohingya group in northern Rakhine State, in violation of its obligations under the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide,” said ICJ President Yuji Iwasawa.

Myanmar’s ​security forces killed ‌thousands of members ​of ⁠the Rohingya minority Muslim population and committed ‌widespread sexual violence, judges ‌at the World ‌Court ⁠ruled on ⁠Thursday (November 19, 2026).

The death toll announcement came early in a three-hour sitting to read out the International Court of Justice’s decision on whether Myanmar committed genocide in a brutal offensive against the Rohingya nearly a decade ago.

Judges ruled ‌that actions ‌by ‌Myanmar ⁠against ⁠the Rohingya in 2017 had ​the “intention ‌to destroy” a substantial ‌part of ​the Muslim minority population, ⁠meeting the ‌legal threshold for genocide.

Myanmar’s soldiers killed and raped Rohingya, committed violence against children, and destroyed Rohingya villages and settlements, the top UN court said.

They “killed thousands of Rohingya civilians, perpetrated widespread acts of sexual violence as well as acts of extreme violence against children, and attacked fleeing Rohingya as they sought to flee in large numbers to Bangladesh,” said Mr. Iwasawa.

articles.title: Replace Russian junk with American weapons system: U.S. lawmaker to India
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Michael Baumgartner made the remarks on Capitol Hill in the presence of Namgya Khampa, the Deputy Chief of Mission at the Indian Embassy in Washington

India should replace its "legacy ineffective Russian junk” with American weapons systems and also opt for Boeing aircraft over those manufactured by European Airbus Industries, a U.S. Congressman has suggested.

Michael Baumgartner, a Republican from Washington state, made the remarks at Deepavali celebrations on Capitol Hill on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) in the presence of Namgya Khampa, the Deputy Chief of Mission at the Indian Embassy in Washington.

The Deepavali celebrations were hosted by BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha, Asian American Hotel Owners Association, Hindu American Foundations, Srimad Rajchandra Mission Dharampur, Sikhs of America, Art of Living, Foundations of Jain Associations in North America and the U.S. Indian Community Foundation.

As a member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, Mr. Baumgartner said he regularly engages with diplomats from the Indian Embassy as the two countries seek to strengthen relations across economic and security issues.

“I was pleased to again express my thoughts that the more U.S. exports to India — from weapons systems to replace their legacy ineffective Russian junk to Boeing airplanes that are superior to Airbus to the world’s best lentils from the Palouse — the better it is for our two great countries,” Mr. Baumgartner said in a post on X.
Mr. Baumgartner also raised the issue of disruptions during Deepavali celebrations in his home state of Washington.

“A couple weeks back some attention-seeking racist morons disrupted a Diwali celebration in my home state of Washington. This evening, I was pleased to attend the Diwali celebration at the US Capitol,” he said.

The Deepavali celebrations were also attended by the U.S. Congresswoman-elect Pia Dandiya, Congresspersons Grace Meng, Suhas Subramanyam, Shri Thanedar, Nick LaLota, Jonathan Jackson, Raja Krishnamoorthi, Norma Torres, Pete Sessions, Deborah Ross, Buddy Carter, Michael Guest, among others.
Scott Colom, who scripted history by becoming the first black Senator from Mississippi in 146 years, also lit the traditional lamp at the Deepavali celebrations.

articles.title: GTA VI generates record $1.1 billion pre-order revenue
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: With record pre-orders and broad market reach, GTA VI is positioned to dominate digital engagement through the end of the year

As Grand Theft Auto (GTA) VI officially launches today , November 19, 2026, a market intelligence report from Sensor Tower highlights an unprecedented shift in consumer engagement and industry revenue.

According to Sensor Tower’s report, the title generated $1.1 billion in pre-order revenue globally across PlayStation and Xbox consoles prior to release, with 11.3 million copies sold. This accomplishment marks the largest pre-launch revenue total on record.

The analytics firms project that total sales could reach $3.2 billion by the end of 2026. Beyond financial performance, the report forecasts a noticeable reallocation of consumer attention across the broader digital landscape.
Daily active user metrics across competing games and entertainment platforms are expected to see a measurable decline as players engage with the new release.
Sensor Tower estimates the average GTA VI player age at approximately 34 years old. This audience displays high companion engagement on second-screen platforms, including Discord, TikTok, and Twitch.
With record pre-orders and broad market reach, GTA VI is positioned to dominate digital engagement through the end of the year.

articles.title: Jensen Huang | AI rainmaker meets his Waterloo

fullParagraphs: The Nvidia chief’s abrupt exit marks a stunning fall from grace for the man who built the hardware foundation of the AI revolution, forged deep ties with Silicon Valley’s tech leaders and expanded the company’s reach across every layer of the AI stack

“In another life, Jensen Huang might have been a teacher,” says Tae Kim in his book The Nvidia Way . Whether he likes it or not, the Nvidia co-founder’s reality has now been reset, forcing him back to his idiosyncratic style of solving problems: diagramming on a whiteboard. But this time he won’t get a clean start as the scandal-hit former chief of Nvidia will face intense scrutiny over his affair with a Chinese businesswoman who is at the centre of an alleged spy scandal.

Within days of reports emerging about Mr. Huang’s affair with Alice Huang , The New York Times reported a second relationship, with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s head of healthcare and one of his direct reports. By then, the controversy had come to a head, forcing Mr. Huang to resign as CEO of Nvidia, the company he had built from scratch.

fullParagraphs: `Koti Deepotsavam’ will be conducted in a traditional manner at Srisailam as part of the ongoing Karthika Masam celebrations. The event will take place on the grounds opposite Agama Pathashala (Vedic School) at 6 p.m. A special stage is being prepared for the event.

Srisailam temple trust board chairman Pothugunta Ramesh Naidu and Executive Officer M. Srinivasa Rao said a devotional musical concert will be presented by renowned playback singer Naguru Babu (Mano) and his troupe, featuring several other prominent singers.

Mr Ramesh Naidu said the `deepam’ (lamp) holds great significance in Vedic tradition. According to our tradition, the flame of a lamp is considered a symbol of the `yajna-agni’ (sacrificial fire). It is for this reason that the Koti Deepotsavam is being organized in accordance with traditional customs, he said.

articles.title: Harish questions Uttam’s silence over AP’s plan to divert 2 TMC of water daily from Nagarjunasagar
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: BRS leader questions the need for a high-capacity tunnel when Andhra Pradesh claims it intends to draw only eight to nine TMC; warns of threat to Hyderabad’s drinking water supply

Former Irrigation Minister T. Harish Rao questioned the State government, particularly Irrigation Minister N. Uttam Kumar Reddy, over silence on Andhra Pradesh’s proposed diversion of two thousand million cubic feet (TMC) of water a day from Nagarjunasagar Project (NSP), alleging that the Congress government had failed to protect Telangana’s interests despite being aware of the project for several months.

He warned that diversion on such a scale could severely deplete Nagarjunasagar, threatening drinking water and irrigation supplies in Nalgonda district and Hyderabad. He claimed that Hyderabad, which depends significantly on Nagarjunasagar for drinking water, could face a severe water crisis, potentially forcing residents to migrate.

Targeting Mr. Uttam Kumar Reddy, who represents Nalgonda district, and holds the Irrigation portfolio, the Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) Legislature Party Deputy Floor leader questioned how the Minister remained unaware of the project when survey and mobilisation activities had allegedly been underway for nearly a year.
He said Andhra Pradesh had issued a Government Order on August 4, 2026, and demanded to know why the Telangana government had failed to intervene even after more than three months.

“Mr. Reddy represents the very district whose drinking water and irrigation interests are at stake. What has he been doing all these days? Was the government asleep while Andhra Pradesh was proceeding with the project?” he asked.

Referring to Roads and Buildings Minister Komatireddy Venkat Reddy’s alleged remarks that he had reprimanded engineering officials for failing to bring the project to the government’s notice, Mr. Harish Rao said the statement itself amounted to an admission of the Congress government’s failure to monitor developments at Nagarjunasagar.

Mr. Rao also criticised the government for citing the control of the Krishna River Management Board (KRMB) and the deployment of Central Reserve Police Force personnel at Nagarjunasagar as reasons for its inability to intervene.
He demanded that the Chief Minister and the Irrigation Minister explain what steps had been taken to stop the proposed diversion and protect Telangana’s drinking water and irrigation interests.

articles.title: Set up Jain development corporation, Joshi tells State govt.
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Union Minister for Education, Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution says it is necessary to address the socio-economic and educational needs of the community

Union Minister for Education, Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution Pralhad Joshi has urged the State government to establish a Jain Development Corporation to address the socio-economic and educational needs of the Jain community in the State.

In a letter to Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, which has been released to the media, Mr. Joshi highlighted a set of demands raised by Jain organisations, including the All India Bhattaraka Jain Matha Parishad.

The letter noted that the Jain community, estimated to have a population of over 20 lakh in Karnataka, has been seeking measures to improve the educational and economic conditions of its members, particularly those in rural areas.

Among the demands are the establishment of a dedicated development corporation, legal measures to ensure the safety of Jain monks and nuns during their travels and financial assistance for pilgrims visiting the Jain shrine of Sri Sammed Shikharji.

The representations are also seeking the conservation and development of historical Jain pilgrimage centres in the State, scholarships for Jain students and the establishment of hostels at the district and taluk levels.
Mr. Joshi said that the State government should consider the demands and take steps to address them.
He also referred to the threat by Jain monk Acharya Gunadharanandi to undertake a Sallekhana Vrata in support of the community’s demands.

articles.title: Lokesh pledges continued support, post-recovery care for Raptadu attack survivor
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Minister for Education Nara Lokesh has expressed happiness over the remarkable recovery of the girl injured in the Raptadu attack, assuring that he would stand by her until she fully recovers physically and emotionally.

“My daughter [Raptadu attack survivor] is a fighter. I will stand by her until she fully recovers and returns to a normal, happy life,” Mr. Lokesh said after reviewing her health condition with doctors at Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru, through a video conference from his Undavalli residence on Wednesday.

Doctors informed the Minister that the girl was making significant progress and could be discharged from the hospital soon. They said she was now breathing independently without ventilator support, had stable oxygen levels and had resumed eating normally. Her major wounds had healed, and the sutures had been removed, while treatment for minor injuries continued.

The medical team also informed him that the girl had started walking with assistance and was gradually increasing her mobility. She could hold a glass of water with her right hand, while rehabilitation exercises were underway to help her regain the ability to write. Her memory and cognitive responses were also showing encouraging improvement.
Recalling an emotional moment, doctors said the girl had recently smiled when they asked her to do so, indicating growing confidence and progress in her recovery.

Mr. Lokesh said her well-being remained his highest priority and emphasised that recovery would extend beyond hospital discharge. He stressed the need for sustained psychological counselling, physical rehabilitation and continued medical supervision to help her overcome the trauma and regain confidence.

Responding to the doctors’ recommendations, the Minister directed officials to ensure comprehensive post-discharge care. A mental health professional would be made available locally, while a dedicated rehabilitation therapist would be arranged in coordination with the Government General Hospital, Anantapur, he said and asked Manipal Hospital doctors to prepare a detailed follow-up plan covering orthopaedic treatment, physiotherapy and any further surgical procedures, if required.
The Minister assured the girl’s family that they would receive continued support and would not be left to face the challenges of recovery alone.

Mr. Lokesh also expressed heartfelt gratitude to the doctors, nurses and medical staff at Manipal Hospital for their dedicated efforts in saving the girl’s life. He acknowledged the timely initial treatment provided by doctors in Anantapur as well.

articles.title: SEC notifies third phase of elections to Gram Panchayats in A.P. on Dec. 2
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Nominations from November 21 to 23; scrutiny on November 24; appeals against rejection of nominations to be filed before 5 p.m. on November 25; polling and counting of votes on December 2

The State Election Commission on Thursday issued the notification for the third phase elections to Gram Panchayats (GPs) in exercise of powers conferred under Article 243-K of the Constitution of India and Sections 13 (2) and 14 (2) of AP Panchayat Raj Act, 1994.
State Election Commissioner Anil Chandra Punetha announced that, as per the schedule, nominations will be received by the Returning Officers from November 21 to 23.
The nominations will be scrutinised on November 24 and appeals against the rejection of nominations have to be filed before the Revenue Divisional Officer concerned before 5 p.m. on November 25.

November 26 and 27 have been fixed as the dates for disposal of appeals, and withdrawal of candidatures (up to 3 p.m.) respectively. The final list of candidates will be published after 3 p.m. on November 27.

Polling will be conducted wherever required, from 7 a.m. to 1 p.m. on December 2. The votes will be counted starting at 2 p.m. on December 2 and results declared soon after the completion of counting.
Re-polling, if necessary, will be conducted on December 3.

Mr. Punetha directed the Collectors and District Election Authorities not to issue any election notice in respect of a GP or any particular post therein, where any court of law passed an order staying or restraining the conduct of election to such GP or to any particular post therein, or where the conduct of election is not feasible due to administrative or legal impediments.
In GPs, where a re-poll is conducted, the election of the Upa-Sarpanch should be conducted only after the declaration of the results of such re-poll on the specified date.

Roughly one-third of these centres focus on generative or . State initiatives such as the IT Policy 2025-30, the ₹300 crore Nipuna Karnataka skilling programme and Beyond Bengaluru clusters aim to support these goals, said Priyank Kharge, Minister for Home, Electronics, IT&BT, Government of Karnataka, while unveiling the report.

articles.title: OMCs achieve 0.08% biodiesel blending in H1, lower than target; cite feedstock shortage
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: In the fiscal year 2025-26, OMCs had achieved an overall biodiesel blending of 0.18%

India’s three state-owned oil marketing companies (OMCs) – Indian Oil Corporation, Hindustan Petroleum Corporation and Bharat Petroleum Corporation – achieved an overall biodiesel blending of just 0.08% in the first half of FY27, “significantly below” the indicative target of 5% by 2030, citing limited feedstock availability.
Biodiesel is produced from various feedstocks, including non-edible vegetable oils, animal fat and recycled cooking oil.

Between April and September 2026, the three OMCs sold approximately 4,900 crore litres of diesel. Of this, more than 4,700 crore litres were sold without any biodiesel blending. The remaining 200 crore litres comprised diesel blended with approximately four crore litres of biodiesel, translating into an average blending rate of 2% in the blended portion, they said in a joint statement.
Consequently, biodiesel accounted for 0.08% of the total diesel sold by the OMCs during the six-month period.
The performance also marks a decline from FY26, when the three companies achieved an overall biodiesel blending rate of 0.18%.

The OMCs reiterated that biodiesel-blended diesel conforms to Bureau of Indian Standards specification BIS 1460, which prescribes requirements for automotive diesel fuel, and is covered under the publicly notified National Policy on Biofuels.

They also pointed out that biodiesel blending is an established global practice, with countries such as Indonesia, Malaysia and Brazil adopting blending levels ranging from 10% to 50%, depending on feedstock availability.

articles.title: New terminal of Belagavi Airport may open by year-end
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: MP Jagadish Shettar says Prime Minister will be invited for inauguration
Work on the second terminal of the Belagavi Airport at Sambra is nearly completed. It can begin operations by year-end, BJP MP Jagadish Shettar said in Belagavi on Wednesday.
“Prime Minister Narendra Modi is likely to inaugurate it in December,” he told officers during an inspection of the works.
He asked officials to expedite work on various sections of the project.

“The new terminal is designed to handle around 1,200 passengers at a time, twice the capacity of the existing terminal. The old terminal is around 3,600 sq m and is facing pressure from increasing passenger traffic,” he said.

“The new building will feature modern passenger amenities and architecture inspired by the historic Kamal Basadi. The project aims to upgrade the airport’s infrastructure to international standards. The foundation stone was virtually laid by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in 2024,” he said.
The MP also chaired the Airport Advisory Committee meeting where flight connectivity, passenger facilities, transport arrangements and future expansion plans were discussed.

He observed that the number of flights has come down. “Currently, only IndiGo operates flights connecting Belagavi with Delhi, Navi Mumbai, Hyderabad and Bengaluru. The number of operators and flights should increase,” he said.

He suggested that the Belagavi-Delhi service, which currently operates four days a week, be made daily. He also told officers to spread awareness about the connecting flights to Ahmedabad via Navi Mumbai, as it can benefit users.
He reprimanded the AAI officials for not inviting Indian Air Force officials to the meeting, where crucial plans of acquisition of around 15 acres of land for future airport expansion were discussed.
The MP urged the Kittur Channamma Road Transport Corporation to introduce bus services connecting the city with the airport, ensuring convenient and affordable transport for passengers.
Mr. Shettar asked officers to resolve the issue of authorities not allowing autorickshaws inside the parking lot of the airport.
He stressed the need for daily flights to Bengaluru during the Winter Session of the State Legislature and asked officers to coordinate with airline operators, said a release.
